researcher_notes: Opus full-redo pass. THIRTEEN source files: nine product datasheets carrying real VDI 2198 Typenblätter — `DE_tb_c_matic_8925_dt_e_1025_view.pdf` (C-MATIC 10/15), `DE_tb_c_matic_hp_10_8928_dt_a_0523_view.pdf` (C-MATIC HP 10), `DE_tb_l_matic_ac_1170_dt_c_1024_view.pdf` (L-MATIC AC 1.2/1.6 t × 2 mast groups), `DE_tb_l_matic_ac_k_1171_dt_b_1225_view.pdf` (L-MATIC 12/16 AC k), `DE_tb_l_matic_core_1195_01_dt_b_0425_view.pdf` (L-MATIC core), `DE_tb_l_matic_hd_hdk_1173_01_dt_d_0524_view.pdf` (L-MATIC HD / HD k), `DE_tb_l_matic_br133_de_a_0516.pdf` (legacy L-MATIC BR 133, 2016), `DE_tb_p_matic_br1190_dt_a_0416.pdf` (legacy P-MATIC BR 1190, 2016), `DE_tb_r_matic_k_5190_dt_a_0425_view.pdf` (R-MATIC 12/17/25 k) — plus `EN_ds_k_matic_5231_en_a_0224_view.pdf` (K-MATIC, 3 mast configs), `EN_ds_r_matic_1120_en_b_0623_view.pdf` (R-MATIC, 4 configs, 'based on R16 HD'), and two overview brochures, `EN_p_robotics_en_a_0216.pdf` and `b_automatisierungsloesungen_dt_a_1023_view.pdf`. THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT FINDING OF THIS GROUP IS NOT A FIELD VALUE — it is that several Linde MATIC models and several STILL iGo models are demonstrably the SAME PHYSICAL MACHINE under two KION Group brands, evidenced by identical VDI Typenblatt values down to battery weights and footnote wording. See `kion_platform_sharing` below; it needs a Tech Lead decision before either brand's rows are enriched further. Second structural finding: the whole legacy MATIC line is Balyo-powered (`DE_tb_p_matic_br1190_dt_a_0416.pdf` p.2 row 1.1 literally reads 'LINDE/BALYO'), and Balyo is a separate company in the DB. Nothing written to Airtable.

kion_platform_sharing.claim: Linde MATIC and STILL iGo are in several cases the same vehicle under two brands. Both companies are KION Group brands and both have their own DB rows, so the matching engine currently treats one factory's machine as two independent suppliers.

evidence.pair: STILL EXV iGo  ==  Linde L-MATIC HD k
evidence.detail: Compare `iGo_systems_DE_TD.pdf` p.6 (STILL, processed earlier in this same session) against `DE_tb_l_matic_hd_hdk_1173_01_dt_d_0524_view.pdf` p.2 column 'L-MATIC HD k'. Identical on: Eigengewicht 1550 kg; h1 1915; h2 150; h3 2844; h4 3364; h13 86; l1 2208; l2 966; b1 1000; Gabelzinken 71/182/1250; b3 780; b5 560; b4 255; m2 20; Ast (800×1200 längs) 2925; Wenderadius 1744; Energieverbrauch 0.925 kWh/h; battery 3PzS 24 V/375 Ah, 333 kg; Fahrmotor 2.3 kW; Hubmotor 3.2 kW. Both sheets even carry the SAME footnote, '+75 mm mit 4PzS'. Two independently published Typenblätter do not agree on nineteen values by coincidence.

evidence.detail: DB `STILL AXV 12 iGo` holds max_payload 1200, lifting_height 1844, min_aisle_width 2480. `DE_tb_l_matic_core_1195_01_dt_b_0425_view.pdf` p.2: Q 1,2 t; Hub h3 1844 mm; Arbeitsgangbreite 800×1200 längs, automatisierter Betrieb, Ast 2480 mm. All three match exactly, including the unusual 1844.

evidence.pair: STILL ACH 06 iGo  ==  a 600 kg C-MATIC variant
evidence.detail: Earlier in this session I flagged STILL's ACH 06 (600 kg) as unsupported, because STILL's own 2026 material only ever says 'ACH 10-15 iGo'. `b_automatisierungsloesungen_dt_a_1023_view.pdf` p.3 resolves it from the Linde side: the AMR column reads 'Traglasten von 600 kg, 1.000 kg und 1.500 kg'. A 600 kg member of this platform therefore does exist — it is simply absent from the C-MATIC Typenblatt in `DE_tb_c_matic_8925…pdf`, which covers only the 10 and 15. RETRACTS the 'possibly discontinued' flag on STILL ACH 06 iGo.

evidence.pair: STILL FM-X iGo series  ~~  Linde R-MATIC k series (same chassis, different ratings)
evidence.strength: same platform, NOT the same product
evidence.detail: `DE_tb_r_matic_k_5190_dt_a_0425_view.pdf` p.5 and `iGo_systems_DE_TD.pdf` p.10 share the chassis: Radstand 1275/1453/1669 in both; tyres Ø360×130 front and Ø285×100 rear (Ø360×140 / Ø350×100 on the largest); b11 1167; b4 920; Fahrmotor 6.5 kW; Hubmotor 14 kW; h1 2450; Freihub 1925. But the payload ratings differ per brand: FM-X 12/17/25 iGo = 1100/1600/2400 kg vs R-MATIC 12/17/25 k = 1070/1550/2330 kg. Same truck, differently derated (or differently rounded) by each brand. `EN_ds_r_matic_1120_en_b_0623_view.pdf` (R-MATIC 'based on R16 HD') shares the same chassis constants too.

evidence.pair: STILL MX-X iGo  ~~  Linde K-MATIC (same VNA platform)
evidence.detail: `EN_ds_k_matic_5231_en_a_0224_view.pdf` p.2 and `iGo_systems_DE_TD.pdf` p.12 share: h6 (overhead guard/cabin) 2555; h7 (seat height) 460; fork dimensions 50/120/1250; fork carriage width b3 710; fork spread b5 470/640; m1 40; m2 87; drive motor 7.0 kW S2 60 min; lift motor 24.0 kW S3 15 %; 80 V PzS batteries weighing 1863 kg and 2178 kg. Ratings differ slightly (K-MATIC 1.45 t / Ast 1850–2000; MX-X iGo 1.4 t / Ast 1800).

kion_platform_sharing.recommendation: DO NOT enrich either brand's rows further until the Tech Lead rules on how KION-internal rebadges should be modelled. This is the same class of question already settled for Magazino SOTO ↔ Jungheinrich ('extra brand', separate Product row sharing one Base Model), and the Entity Model's Product/Base-Model split is designed for exactly this. The operational risk if it is left alone: a tender shortlist that looks like two competing offers is really one manufacturer twice, which distorts any 'number of qualifying suppliers' judgement. Note this cuts both ways — it also means a spec published by only one of the two brands can legitimately be used to fill the other's NULLs, once the base-model link exists.

company_wide_context.notes: MUST be fanned out per base model. `infrastructure_free` has ONE clear exception that must not be over-written: the C-MATIC (8925) navigates by QR codes on the floor (`DE_tb_c_matic_8925…pdf` p.1 and p.5, 'Navigation mit QR-Codes mit max. Intervall von 1400 × 1400 mm'), which IS floor infrastructure — the DB correctly holds infrastructure_free=0 for it. BALYO RELATIONSHIP — flagged for the Tech Lead: `DE_tb_p_matic_br1190_dt_a_0416.pdf` p.2 and `DE_tb_l_matic_br133_de_a_0516.pdf` p.2 both print row '1.1 Hersteller (Kurzbezeichnung): **LINDE/BALYO**', and the P-MATIC text on p.1 names the navigation 'die zuverlässige Geo-Navigation "Driven by BALYO"'. Balyo exists as a separate company in the DB with its own products. The newer 2023–2025 datasheets (C-MATIC HP, L-MATIC core/AC k, R-MATIC k) no longer print the BALYO name, so this may be a legacy arrangement — but the two 2016 sheets are unambiguous, and the same 'geoguidance' framing survives in `EN_p_robotics_en_a_0216.pdf` p.9 ('Linde-MATIC geoguidance'). Same modelling question as Magazino↔Jungheinrich, from the technology-licence side rather than the rebadge side.

products.notes: `rotation_capable = true` is a GENUINE positive here and worth contrasting with the many false ones in this corpus: the source says the PLATFORM rotates to orient the LOAD ('Drehbare Plattform zur Ausrichtung der Ladung', p.1; 'Drehen … der Last mit 90°, 180° und 270°', p.5) — the carried item is turned, not merely the chassis. Same distinction as Kivnon K07 earlier in this session. The DB already holds nothing for this field, so it is a fill, not an override. AISLE WIDTH — the recurring AMR gap, with an unusually precise value going to waste: p.2 row '4.34 Arbeitsgangbreite … Ast (mm) 1897' (footnote: 'Einschließlich 200 mm (min.) Sicherheitsabstand'; with the adapter plate, 1642/1762/1898 mm depending on pallet). AP0 has no aisle-width field in AMR scope, so none of it is storable — while the identical machine sold as a STILL ACH 10/15 iGo has 1897 stored in the FORKLIFT-scope `min_aisle_width` field on its AMR row. That is the gap and its corruption, visible on the same machine from both sides. FLOOR/STEP LIMITS, unstorable: footnote 6, 'Zulässige Stufenhöhe bei Nenngeschwindigkeit ≤ 5 mm – mit reduzierter Geschwindigkeit ≤ 10 mm, überfahrbarer Spalt bei Nenngeschwindigkeit ≤ 5 mm – mit reduzierter Geschwindigkeit ≤ 30 mm'. Also unstorable: the QR-code grid pitch requirement, p.4 'Der maximale QR-Code Abstand (CUD) ist begrenzt auf 1500 mm. Der Standard-CUD beträgt 1400 mm.' — a hard site-preparation constraint. max_speed: DB holds 1.2; p.2 row 5.1 gives '4,3/5,4 km/h' laden/unladen → 1.19 / 1.50 m/s. The DB's 1.2 is the LADEN figure correctly converted; noted rather than flagged, but be aware other suppliers' max_speed values in this DB are unladen figures, so the comparison is not apples-to-apples.

products.notes: PAYLOAD/LIFT MATRIX that AP0 collapses: the four columns are (1.2 t, h3 1924), (1.6 t, h3 1844), (1.2 t, h3 4224), (1.6 t, h3 4144). So the 1.6 t rating costs 80 mm of lift in both mast groups — a small but real payload/height coupling, and the DB's 4200 mm sits between the two high-mast values (it matches p.1's marketing round-off, '→ Tragkraft bis zu 1,6 t und Hubhöhe bis zu 4,2 m', which is really the 1.2 t figure of 4224). Strictly, a 1.6 t L-MATIC AC lifts 4144 mm, not 4200. Flagged as an accuracy note rather than a conflict because the difference is 56 mm. VARIANT COMPLETION NOT PROPOSED for the 1.2 t builds: they would be three additional rows differing only in payload and ~80 mm of lift, and the two mast groups are already representable. A reviewer may disagree; the numbers are all here. AP0 GAP (recurring, now 11+): p.2 row '4.35 Wenderadius Wa (mm) 1668 | 2033' — explicit radius, no Forklift-scope field. Dead weight 2020–2275 kg (row 2.1). Fork spread b5 314/682 mm (row 4.25) — an adjustable spread with no stated mechanism, the recurring `fork_spread` gap. Sound pressure <70 dB(A) (row 10.7).

The DB stores the mast's lift (10274), but the height at which this truck can actually place a pallet under automation is 9974 mm — 300 mm lower. For a K.O. field this is the difference between winning and failing a 10 m high-bay tender. The second mast group's top option is h3 10474 / h* 10174, so a 10 m automated storage height IS achievable, just not with the mast the DB's number implies. Recommend the reviewer decide globally whether `lifting_height` means Hub or Einlagerhöhe; this datasheet makes the case that it should be the latter for automated trucks.
